import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import io
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Prepare the data
csv_data = """survived,pclass,sex,age,sibsp,parch,fare,embarked,class,who,adult_male,deck,embark_town,alive,alone
0,3,male,22.0,1,0,7.25,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,False
1,1,female,38.0,1,0,71.2833,C,First,woman,False,C,Cherbourg,yes,False
1,3,female,26.0,0,0,7.925,S,Third,woman,False,,Southampton,yes,True
1,1,female,35.0,1,0,53.1,S,First,woman,False,C,Southampton,yes,False
0,3,male,35.0,0,0,8.05,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,True
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set visualization style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="muted")

# Create the plot
# A catplot with kind='bar' is excellent for comparing a metric (in this case, the mean of 'survived',
# which is the survival rate) across different categorical variables.
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    kind="bar",
    x="class",
    y="survived",
    hue="sex",
    height=6,
    aspect=1.3,
    palette={"male": "#3498db", "female": "#e74c3c"},
    legend=False,  # We will create a custom legend
    order=["First", "Third"] # Explicitly order the classes
)

# Access the underlying axes for customization
ax = g.ax

# Set titles and labels for clarity
ax.set_title("Titanic Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex", fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel("Passenger Class", fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel("Survival Rate", fontsize=12)

# Format the y-axis to show percentages
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1.0))
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.1)

# Add data labels on top of each bar
for p in ax.patches:
    height = p.get_height()
    if height > 0:
        ax.annotate(f'{height:.0%}',
                    (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., height),
                    ha='center',
                    va='center',
                    xytext=(0, 9),
                    textcoords='offset points',
                    fontsize=11,
                    color='dimgray')

# Improve the legend
ax.legend(title='Sex', loc='upper left', frameon=True)

# Add a descriptive subtitle
plt.figtext(0.5, 0.95, "Based on the provided sample dataset", ha="center", fontsize=10, style='italic')

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.95])

# Save the resulting visualization
plt.savefig("output.png", dpi=300)

plt.close()
